title: fix(test): cross-platform color rounding in conversions
author: cscnk52
summary: Despite the title, this changes production color-conversion math: it replaces std atan2/sin/cos/cbrt/powf with the `libm` crate and powi with multiplication, so Windows test output matches Linux. It adds a new runtime dependency and may change last-digit output and speed on all platforms; part of a Windows-parity cluster (#1247 hashes, #1249 CI matrix, #1119/#1120).
evidence: Master still uses powi/cbrt/atan2 in src/values/color.rs. #541 shows Windows diffs like `40.4543` vs `40.4542`. A commenter on #541 suggested tolerance-based test comparisons instead. No reviews or comments on the PR. Not checked: whether outputs change on Linux, or the perf of libm vs intrinsics.
decision: Is Windows test parity worth adding a `libm` dependency and changing color math on every platform, or should tests use tolerant comparisons (or skip Windows CI)?
